title: Casey Wasserman’s agency rebrands without his name following outcry over Epstein ties
content:
The Wasserman talent agency is rebranding without the name of its founder Casey Wasserman as the outcry over his ties to Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell continues.

Wasserman, 51, already announced his intention to sell the business last month following the publication of flirtatious emails with Maxwell within the latest released files by the U.S. Department of Justice.

Wasserman’s name appears in two emails from 2003 with Maxwell, who is now serving a 20-year prison sentence on sex trafficking charges. He has maintained he had no contact with Maxwell or Epstein in the past 20 years, but said he deeply regrets his correspondence with Maxwell, “which took place over two decades ago, long before her horrific crimes came to light.”

A statement on the agency’s website on Monday confirmed the rebrand to The Team, alongside a new company logo.

“For 24 years, this company has been shaped by our work, our people and our unifying belief in the power of sports, music and entertainment,” the statement read. “That philosophy remains the foundation of who we are — and where we are going. We go forward as we always have: Together.”

United States women’s soccer legend Abby Wambach was one of several star names to leave the agency in the wake of Wasserman’s appearance in the latest tranche of Epstein files. Music star Chappell Roan was another.

Wasserman has faced calls to resign from his position as chair of the LA28 Olympic Committee but retained the backing of organizers last month.

Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass has been one of the most high-profile voices to speak out against him remaining in post, but “I cannot fire him,” she told CNN. “My opinion is that he should step down,” she continued. “That’s not the opinion of the board.”
